item.description: Most seeds are started indoors about 4 to 8 weeks before last frost, but some favorite flowers and vegetables need a longer head start to perform their best.

item.title: Don’t Start Indoor Seeds Too Soon—Here’s Why
item.description: While it sounds smart to give seedlings extra time to grow indoors, it can cause big problems later on.

item.description: Most seeds are started indoors weeks before last frost. But some slow-growing vegetables need extra time indoors to be ready to plant out in spring.

item.title: Indoor Seed Starting: Avoid These Beginner Mistakes
item.description: If you want to be sure your seeds germinate successfully indoors, this checklist will help. These are all the little things that can help or hurt your seed sowing. It also provides a good overview of the steps so you know what to expect as your seeds grow.

item.title: 30 Imaginative Garden Art Ideas Spotted in Real Backyards

item.description: Learn how to grow citrus seeds from oranges, lemons, and more into beautiful houseplants. This simple method ensures reliable germination for your indoor garden.

item.title: 20 Fast-Growing Vegetables in 4-6 Weeks (Spring or Fall)
item.description: Quick-growing vegetables perfect for cool spring and fall growing conditions include leafy greens, carrots, beets, radishes, and peas. Started from seed, many are ready for harvest in just four to six weeks.

item.title: 7 Enchanting Fairy & Miniature Garden Ideas

item.title: How to Plant Asparagus Crowns
item.description: The quickest way to start a new asparagus patch is to plant young living roots known as crowns. In the right location, this perennial vegetable will provide ample yields for years to come.

item.title: How to Grow a Peach Tree From a Pit
item.description: Can you grow a peach tree from a store-bought pit? Yes! Learn the easy way to grow peaches, plums, and cherries with this stone fruit propagation guide.
